system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action/temporal motion overrides a subject plate's static pose. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette: a requested scene color palette governs, whereas an object's incidental color does not recolor the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. A reference sheet's panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

brief.intent: the woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground, cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements

cards.summary: A cinematic character reference sheet for a person in an all-black tactical outfit, featuring a rainy environmental hero shot, studio turnaround views, and close-up detail panels.

subjects.descriptor: adult with short dark undercut hair and a small topknot, wearing an all-black tactical jacket, trousers, and combat boots
attributes: short dark hair shaved at the sides with a small topknot at the back
lean build
thin scar-like mark through one eyebrow
black high-collared tactical jacket with straps and metal buckle details
dark shirt
black cargo trousers
black lace-up combat boots
metallic tag necklace
pose: standing with arms relaxed at the sides in the full-body views
head turned to the left in the hero panel
shown in front, side-profile, and back views

cards.environment: Top panel: rainy nighttime urban walkway with wet reflective pavement, metal railings, and blurred city lights. Lower panels: dark neutral studio backdrop.
cards.lighting: Low-key cinematic lighting; cool blue-gray ambient light with warm amber background highlights in the hero panel and soft directional studio light in the reference panels.
cards.framing: Reference-sheet layout with a wide environmental full-body hero panel, three full-body turnaround panels, and four detail close-ups.

cards.summary: Dark fantasy dragon character reference sheet: one large atmospheric panel of the creature in a volcanic landscape plus labeled turnaround and detail panels (front, side, rear, head close-up, wing membrane, claw and foot, scale detail).

subjects.descriptor: large dark-scaled dragon with membranous wings and multiple swept-back horns
attributes: black to blue-gray overlapping armored scales
crest of long pale-tipped horns angled backward from the skull
smaller spikes running along the neck, back and long tail
large bat-like wings with dark veined membrane
four legs with long pale curved talons
orange eye visible in the head close-up
pose: standing quadrupedally with head lowered in the top panel
wings spread in the front, side and rear views

subjects.descriptor: volcanic rocky terrain with mist and shallow water in the top panel
attributes: jagged dark rock formations
orange-red glow suggesting lava or fire
damp reflective ground
low fog
plain dark gray studio-like backdrop in the smaller panels

cards.environment: Top panel: misty volcanic rock landscape with lava glow and shallow water. Lower panels: plain dark gray backdrop.
cards.lighting: Low-key, dramatic side and rim lighting with cool blue-gray highlights and warm orange background glow in the top panel
cards.framing: Multi-panel contact sheet with one wide hero image on top and a two-row grid of smaller labeled panels beneath
cards.style: dark fantasy photorealistic CG creature concept art
